Subject: Private deployment: edge connectivity & segmentation (diagram attached)

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We are moving forward with a pilot of Redwood Private in our West-2 on‑prem cluster and wanted to get a focused architecture review on edge connectivity and segmentation before we enable the control-plane endpoints.

Attached is a preliminary network diagram (acme-edge-vpc-diagram-v2.pdf) and a short connectivity matrix. Our primary asks:
- Validate the proposed demarcation between the control plane (Redwood management plane) and local data plane (model inference nodes).
- Confirm recommended ingress/egress rules and NAT placement for air‑gapped subnets.
- Discuss certificate distribution and where Redwood expects outbound TLS connections (if any) from the control plane.
- Review what monitoring/health traffic needs to cross the boundary and recommended ports.

Can you loop in the infra/network folks and share a proposed time for a 45‑minute review this week? Also flag any obvious blockers so we can adjust the diagram before the meeting.

Thanks,
Jessica Leung
Director, Cloud Solutions
Acme Cloud Solutions

Jessica — thanks for the diagram and the matrix, this is helpful. Looping in our infra and network owners to review technical constraints; I’ve attached an initial checklist (redwood-onprem-checklist.docx) with the things we typically validate.

High level agenda for the call:
1) Walk the diagram and confirm demarcation: control plane endpoints (managed by Redwood) vs data plane (customer-sited inference nodes).
2) Ports & egress: what needs to be allowed outbound from the control plane and data plane (list & justification).
3) Certificate & identity: how certs will be provisioned/rotated (ACME or customer-supplied), and whether an internal PKI is required.
4) Monitoring & audit: which metrics/traces are shipped out and whether push model is acceptable or we need a pull/Aggregator behind the boundary.
5) Pilot cutover window & rollback plan.

Proposed times: Wed 05/16 09:30-10:15 PT or Thu 05/17 13:00-13:45 PT. If neither works, suggest alternatives.

Next steps: Aditya, Diego, Neha — can you review the attached checklist and add items inline? I’ll book the slot once we agree.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Jessica Leung <jessica.leung@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 May 2028 10:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: edge connectivity & segmentation (diagram attached)

Jessica / team — quick pass from infra/networking from our side. I left inline notes on the diagram PDF and the checklist but summarizing the key items we should cover in the review.

Summary of technical notes (short):
- Control plane <> data plane boundary: we recommend a strict uni-directional control channel where the control plane (management API) initiates authenticated gRPC to an agent in the data plane over TLS 1.3. The agent should be in a subnet that has outbound-only access to the control-plane Egress IPs.
- Ingress patterns: we do NOT require public inbound on the data-plane layer. All admin/management traffic should be outbound from customer network to Redwood control endpoints. If Acme requires inbound (due to strict firewall posture), we can support a customer-managed reverse proxy, but that increases operational surface.
- Ports & protocols (recommended minimal):
  * 443 TCP (HTTPS) — control plane API and certificate provisioning
  * 8443 TCP — optional admin API for debug flows (restrict to mgmt CIDR)
  * 2379 TCP — etcd (if you run a shared etcd; prefer cross-site peering only if necessary)
  * 10250 TCP — Kubelet (if using k8s nodes for inference; limit to controller IPs)
- NAT placement: Prefer placing NAT at the edge subnets so outbound connections preserve source IP for egress allowlists. Avoid hairpin NAT for control->data local traffic.
- KV cache replication & model weights: If you plan to pre-warm model weights across nodes we recommend using an internal object-store (S3 compatible) in the on‑prem environment rather than allowing large pulls over the Internet.
- Certificate distribution: We support both ACME (Let's Encrypt) and enterprise-supplied certs. For air‑gapped sites with no outbound ACME, customer-supplied certs or an internal ACME gateway is required.
- Observability: Our agent emits health heartbeats and aggregated metrics over HTTPS. Review which metrics you want forwarded offsite — most customers ship aggregated telemetry only.

Action items for the call:
- Confirm list of CIDRs for control-plane egress allowlist (we will provide a short-lived set during pilot).
- Decide whether data-plane nodes will pull model artifacts from internal S3 or from Redwood-hosted artifact repository.
- If inbound rules are unavoidable for your posture, provide a justification and we’ll document the hardened reverse-proxy pattern.

I can cover the kernel of the control-plane design on the call; Diego can deep-dive network path and Neha will own the pilot-runbook items.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — very helpful notes. We reviewed the annotated diagram and the checklist with our security team this morning. A couple of quick agreements and asks before we schedule the pilot cutover window:
- Agreement: outbound-only control channel and NAT-at-edge approach is acceptable.
- Action: we will provide the control-plane allowlist CIDRs by EOD Monday (ACME-9123).
- Request: can Redwood provide a short runbook for certificate rotation in air‑gapped mode and a hardened reverse-proxy config (if we go that route)? A sample Nginx/Envoy snippet would be enough.
- Pilot window: target week of 2028-06-05; provisioning lead time ~2 weeks for hardware.

If you can attach the certificate runbook draft and a reverse-proxy example, we’ll mark this thread ready for scheduling. I’ve created the Jira ticket and added the attachments reference.

Best,
Jessica Leung
